title: Rashi Peripherals Ltd - 544119 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Rashi Peripherals Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue up 49% YoY to ₹6,185 cr with PAT up 121%, but inventory build, D/E at 0.76x and a QIP overhang temper the read; supply-side signals are thin.

summary.headline: Rashi Peripherals Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 49% YoY to ₹6,185 crore and PAT grew 121% to ₹131 crore, with H1 PAT up 95%.
summary.overview: Management reported record Q2 and H1 FY27 profits on both standalone and consolidated bases, driven by pricing, mix and the VDA acquisition, which was consolidated for the first time this quarter (about one month of semiconductor contribution as well). Consolidated EBITDA margin was 3.56% in Q2, up 106 bps, and PAT margin was 2.11%, up 69 bps. Management said the H1 inventory build and higher debt (debt-to-equity 0.76x) were deliberate, to secure supply in a constrained market and to fund the Diwali-timing shift. A QIP was flagged as a possible capital-raising step, which an analyst questioned due to dilution of around 15%.

segments.name: Core ICT distribution (PC, accessories, CPUs)
segments.commentary: Management said non-PC products are more than 35-37% of the business and carry better margin. Growth of about 30% in H1 was attributed to price increases, with new initiatives adding about 6% in Q2 (one month of contribution).

segments.name: VDA (system integration, cyber security, cloud, managed services)
segments.commentary: 67% stake acquired; consolidated from Q2 FY27 for about one month per the call (management described it as a first-quarter contribution). Management said it contributes under 2% of revenue at this stage. Intangibles from the acquisition are being amortised, and about ₹12 crore per quarter is now booked as depreciation including amortisation.

segments.name: Semiconductor (RESTAR JV)
segments.commentary: JV with RESTAR Corporation formalised; management targets 3-4x last year's semiconductor numbers in H1 FY27 and says margins are about 2x the company average, though the revenue base is small.

segments.name: Enterprise / AI data centre
segments.commentary: Management chose not to pursue large AI data-centre orders in H1 (more than ₹20,000 crore of orders reportedly placed in one quarter). Target is for enterprise to reach about 20% of business next year.

guidance_outlook: Sustainable EBITDA margin of around 2.75% considered a safe base case for FY29-FY30 once full capex utilisation is reached (for the proposed ₹900 crore raise).
Management expects 10-15% price contribution to growth in H2, plus new initiatives and flattish-to-positive volumes; visibility beyond the next few quarters described as difficult.
Industry growth expected at 10-12% in units; commercial demand expected flat to positive in Jan-Mar, with consumer demand expected to decline.
Interest cost guided to remain at the H1 run-rate, including acquisition debt interest.

Debt-to-equity to be held around 1:1 except for opportunities where ROCE justifies more; current 0.76x includes acquisition debt. Borrowings expected to peak around the September quarter and taper later.
Management said the QIP may not be needed, but any raise would add about ₹1,800-2,000 crore deployable capital, supporting about ₹12,000-15,000 crore of additional revenue.
capex_capacity: QIP of about ₹900 crore was discussed as capital for growth; management said it may not proceed and wants to avoid being capital-constrained.
Company operates 57 branches, 50 service centres and reaches 728 locations across India.
Joint venture with SEMITA (conductor and embedded solutions) formalised to build local design and engineering capability; RESTAR JV to add a design centre in Bangalore (one engineer initially).
Management said it is meeting five Japanese manufacturers in India in the month of the call for semiconductor business.
demand_pricing: India PC market grew about 12% in April-June quarter, led by commercial, education, small business, and premium/AI-capable notebooks.

Price increases (led by DRAM and flash) contributed about 30% of H1 growth; management expects 10-15% price contribution in H2, but noted price flattening and DRAM stock weakness at SK Hynix and Samsung.

Inventory build was attributed to Diwali timing shifting (Diwali 2026 later than 2025's 20 October), pushing one inventory cycle into late September and October; management said consumer softness impact so far is minimal and commercial is about 70% of India's ICT market.
Management said post-COVID price correction of 10-15% was offset by expansion into new products, territories and customers, and expects similar resilience if prices reverse.
Semiconductor distribution market in India estimated at about ₹25,000 crore; management said the Japanese distributors' reach is around 10% of the opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Why was inventory built up strongly if consumer demand is softening, and is the ~15% dilution from a QIP linked to an acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory build was linked to Diwali timing shifting one cycle into late September/October; commercial demand (about 70% of ICT market) is growing and sales continue well. On the QIP, management said it is a precautionary step for growth capital, may not be done at all, and could be done in a calibrated manner.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA margin for FY29-FY30 and how much AI-related exposure is expected over 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said around 2.75% EBITDA margin is a safe long-term base; India industry expected to grow at 10-12% in units; AI demand is at an early stage with large projects at various stages of finalisation.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin resilience and how large is the VDA contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited strong demand, pricing that reduces market bloodbath, about 35-37% non-PC mix with higher margins, and margin-linked KPIs across categories. VDA contributes under 2% of revenue at this stage.

qa_highlights.question: What does the RESTAR JV bring and what are its margins and scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RESTAR is a Japanese semiconductor distributor with a ~US$4 billion group; the JV brings new product lines, design capabilities and access to Japanese manufacturers in India. Margins expected at about 2x company average; semiconductor H1 targeted at 3-4x last year.

qa_highlights.question: How much of pricing versus volume drove growth, and what is the pricing outlook given possible AI-driven price correction?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30% of H1 growth came from price increases, expected at 10-15% in H2. Management expects DRAM/flash prices to stay elevated, though it sees price flattening and volatility beyond that.

qa_highlights.question: What is the depreciation and employee cost run-rate after VDA consolidation, and is peak borrowing reached?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹12 crore per quarter depreciation including intangible amortisation; ESOP amortisation about ₹3.8 crore in the quarter. Gross borrowing is expected to peak around the September quarter and taper later.

risks_watch: Negative cash flow in H1 and debt-to-equity at 0.76x, with inventory unwind needed in H2 to convert working capital into cash (VDA acquisition debt to be serviced).
Price volatility: management sees price flattening and DRAM stock weakness; a post-shortage price correction would hit revenue, though management cited post-COVID precedent of 10-15% drop.
Possible QIP of about ₹900 crore with roughly 15% dilution; an analyst pushed for a more calibrated raise.
Consumer demand softness versus commercial growth; management expects consumer decline and flat-to-positive commercial demand.
Enterprise and AI data-centre business is large-ticket with low ROI per management; management chose not to pursue large orders in H1 and could reconsider in H2.
Integration and reporting of VDA and RESTAR JV; the RESTAR JV is not yet formalised and partner names were not disclosed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and profitability, with a candid tone on the balance sheet (higher debt and negative H1 cash flow explained as deliberate inventory build). Management was cautious on the outlook for consumer demand and price volatility and did not give volume or AI mix guidance beyond general commentary. Some answers were vague, notably on the QIP size and timing and the RESTAR partner names.
key_quotes: Both reflect deliberate choice we built inventory to secure supply in a constrained market.
So the expansion is coming from mix and pricing discipline not only operating leverage.
So in short the impact so far is minuscule.
We do not need these growth capital.

adds.what: Rashi Peripherals adds no new plants or stores; 57 branches, 50 service centres, 728 locations already operating

growth.why: Management expects 10-15% price contribution to growth in H2 plus new initiatives and flattish-to-positive volumes, with industry units guided at 10-12%, but no firm revenue growth % is given and visibility beyond a few quarters is described as difficult.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA margin rose 106 bps to 3.56% in Q2, but management pointed to 10-15% price contribution in H2 and price flattening, and gave no explicit H2 margin guide beyond a ~2.75% long-term base.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plants, stores or branches are planned; the company already runs 57 branches, 50 service centres and 728 locations, and the only capacity-type items are a design centre and JV setup.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects flattish-to-positive volumes in H2 with industry units guided at 10-12%, and commercial demand (about 70% of ICT) is growing, though consumer demand is expected to decline.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not discussed and no new capex is firmly planned; the ~₹900 crore QIP is for growth capital but management said it may not proceed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 PAT was up 95% and Q2 PAT up 121%, but management said visibility beyond a few quarters is difficult and gave no formal numeric revenue guide.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Price flattening, DRAM stock weakness at SK Hynix and Samsung, and consumer decline could hit H2, with H1 operating cash flow negative and borrowings peaking around the September quarter.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Semiconductor (RESTAR JV) targets 3-4x last year's H1 numbers at about 2x company margins, with a Bangalore design centre and five Japanese manufacturer meetings in the call month, though partner names are undisclosed.

rows.label: Enterprise / AI data-centre re-entry
rows.why: Management skipped large AI data-centre orders in H1 (over ₹20,000 crore placed in one quarter) and targets enterprise at about 20% of business next year, so it could reconsider in H2.

rows.label: Working capital unwind and debt peak
rows.why: Working capital days fell to 55 from 61, with borrowings expected to peak around the September quarter and taper after; debt-to-equity is 0.76x against a target of about 1:1.

rows.label: QIP of about ₹900 crore
rows.why: Management said the QIP may not proceed; if done, it would add about ₹1,800-2,000 crore deployable capital and about 15% dilution.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, pricing and profitability (record Q2 and H1 PAT) and cautious on consumer demand, price volatility and the QIP; analysts pressed on the ~15% QIP dilution, the inventory build and the vague RESTAR partner details.
